text: I kept telling everyone that I was fine, and I even laughed at lunch. Once I got home, though, the apartment felt unbearably quiet and I cried without really knowing how to stop.
Today was not a complete disaster, but that is the kindest thing I can say about it. I made it through my responsibilities while feeling empty, tired, and detached from everything around me.
I received the promotion I had worked toward for months. Everyone congratulated me, yet all I could think about was whether I deserved it and how badly I might fail.
The walk was beautiful and the weather was warm, but I could not enjoy either of them. My thoughts kept returning to the argument, and the heaviness followed me home.
I am not as upset as I was yesterday, although I still feel lonely and discouraged. Improvement is happening so slowly that it is difficult to believe things will actually get better.
Nothing especially terrible happened today. Still, every ordinary task felt exhausting, and by evening I had no energy left to speak with anyone.
I smiled through dinner because I did not want my family to worry. Underneath that smile, I felt overwhelmed and frightened about what comes next.
I finished everything on my list, but completing it brought no satisfaction. Instead, I kept wondering why even successful days feel so meaningless lately.
My friend tried to reassure me, and I appreciate the effort. The conversation did not quiet the fear that I am falling behind and disappointing everyone.
For a few minutes this morning I felt hopeful. Then another rejection arrived, and the small amount of confidence I had managed to rebuild disappeared.
I woke up before the alarm, made oatmeal, and reviewed the notes for my afternoon appointment. The appointment lasted forty minutes, and I stopped at the pharmacy on my way back.
The morning was busier than usual because two meetings were moved forward. I completed both, updated the calendar, and spent the remainder of the afternoon answering messages.
I did not dislike the new restaurant, but I would not go out of my way to return. The meal was adequate, service took about an hour, and we left shortly after paying.
My roommate and I discussed how to divide the utility bill. We checked the numbers, transferred our portions, and added next month's due date to the calendar.
The weather changed several times during the day. It rained during my commute, cleared around lunch, and became cloudy again before I returned home.
I spent most of Saturday reorganizing the closet. Some boxes went into storage, some clothes went into a donation bag, and the remaining items went back onto the shelves.
The presentation had both useful and repetitive sections. I took several pages of notes, asked one question near the end, and logged off when the session finished.
I felt tired after work, so I reheated leftovers rather than cooking. I watched one episode of a show, washed the plate, and went to bed at my normal time.
The mechanic said the noise came from a worn belt rather than the engine. The replacement is scheduled for Tuesday and should take approximately two hours.
I am not particularly excited or worried about tomorrow's trip. My bag is packed, the ticket is on my phone, and I have arranged transportation to the station.
This morning began badly when I missed the bus, but the rest of the day surprised me. A colleague helped with my work, we laughed over lunch, and I came home feeling genuinely fortunate.
I was nervous before speaking and stumbled over the opening sentence. Once I settled in, the presentation went well, and I am proud that I continued instead of giving up.
The week was exhausting, so having a quiet evening felt wonderful. I made tea, turned off my phone, and finally gave myself permission to rest without feeling guilty.
I did not win the competition, but I performed far better than I expected. Seeing how much I have improved left me motivated and excited to practice again.
There are still difficult decisions ahead, and I do not have every answer. Even so, today's conversation made me feel supported, capable, and hopeful about handling them.
I almost cancelled dinner because I was tired. I am glad I went: the conversation was warm, the food was lovely, and I laughed more than I have in weeks.
My application was initially returned because a document was missing. I sent the correction this morning and received confirmation that everything is now approved, which was an enormous relief.
I woke up expecting another ordinary birthday, but my friends had planned a small surprise. Their effort made me feel deeply cared for, and I am ending the day with a grateful heart.
Recovery has been slower than I wanted, and today was not perfect. Still, I noticed meaningful progress, completed a task that seemed impossible last week, and felt proud of myself.
The rain cancelled our outdoor plans, but we cooked together and played games at home instead. The change ended up making the evening more relaxed and enjoyable than expected.
